Every per-blob fallback (ScanBlobLinesAtRev, OversizeBlobAtRev, ShowFile and
its limited variants) composed rev^{tree}:prefix+path by running
\`git rev-parse --show-prefix\` before the read itself — one extra subprocess
per blob for an answer that is constant per directory. The loops these
fallbacks serve (over-cap grep-hit validation in search preselection, the
fallback oversize registry) therefore spawned two Git processes per
oversized file where one is inherent.

repoTreePath now memoizes successful RepoPrefix answers per directory for
the process lifetime; failures stay uncached, so a cancelled or broken
first call is retryable. BenchmarkScanBlobLinesAtRevSameRepo drops from
~29-32ms to ~14-16ms per call (Apple M4 Pro), and the new test pins one
--show-prefix spawn per directory across repeated per-blob reads.
